newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain's offshore banking assets rise in Q1 97.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain's offshore banking assets rise in Q1 97.

text.p: Total assets of offshore banking units (OBUs) operating in Bahrain climbed to $68.80 billion in the first quarter of 1997 from $62.50 billion a year earlier, official figures showed on Wednesday.
A Bahrain Monetary Agency (BMA) quarterly bulletin said end-March 1997 assets were also higher than $66.92 billion at end-December 1996. Bahrain is the Gulf's main financial and banking hub.

The BMA, Bahrain's central bank, did not say how many OBUs were operating on the island in 1997, but a BMA official has said there were 46 OBUs operating in 1996 compared with 75 units at the start of the oil boom in mid 1970s.
Assets of commercial banks climbed to 2.719 billion dinars ($7.21 billion) at end-March 1997 from 2.562 billion dinars at end-December 1996.
